fixes.card: Thigh and shank angles are rebuilt
fixes.total_line: All 44 recordings, 100%: every one of the 7,547 converted strides (99.8% of 7,562; the other 15 were never converted), 1,132,050 samples each for thigh and shank. The earlier rebuild was off by about 2° to 58° on average, depending on how far the participant tilts the pelvis.

fixes.grid_caption: Share of each recording's strides whose earlier thigh and shank were wrong (100 everywhere).
fixes.direction: Which way the dependence runs: thigh = hip + pelvis tilt, shank = thigh − knee, foot = shank + ankle. Pelvis, hip, knee and ankle are published by the source; thigh, shank and foot are worked out from them. So a wrong pelvis or hip gives a wrong thigh and shank, and a wrong knee gives a wrong shank only. A wrong thigh never changes the hip or knee.

knock_on.line: A bad thigh does not change the knee angle. The knee is published by the source, not worked out from the thigh. The dependence runs the other way: the shank is thigh − knee.
knock_on.evidence: Shank = thigh − knee holds to rounding in all 7,545 released strides, so the knee is an input, not an output; the published knee sign matched markers in 16 of 16 legs.

fixes.total_line: 12 of 132 power channels (9.1%; 44 recordings × hip, knee, ankle) were not set by a clear rule: 8 left empty and 4 copied. In stride terms: 1,407 of 22,635 stride-joint values left empty (6.2%, 211,050 samples) and 669 copied (3.0%). 16,633 stride-joint values (73.5%, 2,494,950 samples, 96 channels) use a sign set by the moment-times-speed check.
fixes.denominator_text: A stride-joint value is one stride's hip, knee or ankle power (7,545 released strides × 3 joints = 22,635). Of the 124 channels with a sign set, 107 were multiplied by −1 and 17 kept as published. Power is stored in two ways; the 8 recordings stored the second way keep their sign: AB03, 10° incline; AB04, 10° decline; AB04, 5° decline; AB04, 5° incline; AB05, 10° decline; AB05, 5° decline; AB05, level; AB05, 10° incline.
